learningObjective: Explain the elementwise rotation pattern of RoPE and where in the transformer stack it is applied.

canonicalClaims.claim: RoPE rotates pairs of features of Q and K (not V) by position-dependent angles applied pointwise per token; the rotation encodes position such that <RoPE(q, m), RoPE(k, n)> depends only on m - n.
conditions: RoPE is applied after the linear QKV projection and before QK^T.
nonImplications: Does not imply RoPE is applied to V.
Does not imply cross-token reduction; each token's rotation is independent.

misconceptions.claim: RoPE is an additive learned position embedding.
misconceptions.whyWrong: RoPE is a multiplicative rotation in feature space, not an additive embedding.

misconceptions.claim: RoPE is applied to the attention score matrix as an additive relative-position bias.
misconceptions.whyWrong: That description matches ALiBi; RoPE achieves relative position via feature rotation of Q, K.

misconceptions.claim: RoPE requires a reduction over the sequence dimension.
misconceptions.whyWrong: RoPE is pointwise per token; only the token's own features and position matter.

implementationFacts: cos/sin tables are typically precomputed once per max position and cached.
RoPE fuses naturally as a small epilogue on the QKV projection kernel.
Long-context extensions (NTK, YaRN) modify the frequency schedule but keep the rotation structure.
performanceScenarios: RoPE is essentially free per token — a handful of muls/adds and one cos/sin table lookup.
Because K is rotated before caching, KV cache stores post-RoPE K; decode does not re-rotate cached K.
